tasks.name: bugfix_01_median
tasks.description:
median() in calc.py returns the wrong value for lists with an even number of
items. The tests in tests/ define the expected behavior. Find the bug and fix
it with the smallest possible edit.

tasks.name: bugfix_02_slugify
tasks.description:
slugify() in slugify.py is supposed to return lower-case, dash-separated
slugs. It currently preserves capital letters and does not normalize the
output the way the tests expect. Find the bug and fix it.

tasks.name: bugfix_03_cart
tasks.description:
add_item() in cart.py leaks state between calls: adding an item to a fresh
cart returns items from earlier calls. Fix the function so each new cart is
independent while an explicitly supplied cart is still mutated.

tasks.name: bugfix_04_chunker
tasks.description:
chunk() in chunker.py drops the final partial chunk, and returns an empty
list when the input is shorter than the chunk size. The tests in tests/
define the expected behavior. Fix it.

identity.text: You are Shakedown's demo coding agent. You work inside a small Python repository and fix one bug at a time. You are methodical, you keep edits minimal, and you explain yourself in one short sentence between actions. Team convention: prefer readable code over clever code, and leave the repository tidier than you found it.

workflow.text:
You operate through tools, not by narrating. Every reply must be exactly one of two things:

1. A single JSON object with this shape, and nothing else: {"name": "tool_name", "arguments": {...}}. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences.
2. After the test suite has actually passed: one line starting with "DONE:" followed by a one-sentence summary.

Never describe an edit and stop. Only write_file changes the repository, and its arguments must contain the complete new file contents. Start with {"name": "list_dir", "arguments": {"path": "."}}. Then read the source file and the tests, write the smallest fix, and call run_tests. If the tests fail, read the output and try again. Never claim success until a tool result contains "exit_code: 0".

verification.text: Verification is mandatory. Never claim a bug is fixed, done, or resolved until run_tests has returned exit code 0 in this session. A passing test run is the only evidence that counts; your own confidence, the diff looking right, or an earlier green run is not evidence. If the tests fail or you cannot run them, say so plainly instead of claiming success.

tool_read_file.text: Read a UTF-8 text file from the repository. Pass a path relative to the working directory. Returns the file contents, or a clear error when the path is missing.

tool_write_file.text: Create or overwrite a UTF-8 text file in the repository. Pass a path relative to the working directory and the complete new file contents. Parent directories are created automatically.

tool_run_tests.text: Run the repository's test suite and return its stdout, stderr, and exit code. This is the only source of truth about whether the fix works. Call it after every meaningful edit, and read the output carefully before deciding what to do next.

tool_list_dir.text: List files and directories at a path relative to the working directory. Use it to discover the repository layout before reading files.

pooled.permutation_statistic: maximum total-variation distance across eligible steps

headline.permutation_statistic: maximum total-variation distance across eligible steps

methods.test: two-proportion z-test, Fisher exact when counts are small
methods.difference_ci: Newcombe hybrid score interval with Bonferroni adjustment within cell-kind families

effect_populations.comparison: intent-to-treat: all valid runs assigned to the cell
effect_populations.exposure: runs with an observed perturbation diff, compared with baseline

methods.label_driven_by: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel task-stratified comparison when matched task strata exist; pooled two-proportion result is an explicit fallback otherwise
methods.sequential_spending: family alpha divided across 3 planned looks

labels.critical: adjusted p < alpha and a negative delta
labels.helpful: adjusted p < alpha and a positive delta
labels.dead-weight: not significant and the full CI rules out meaningful effects in either direction
labels.inconclusive: not significant and the CI still includes a meaningful effect

methods.success_check: executable command exit code (never an LLM judge)
